structures.name: Conservative Approach
structures.strategy: Minimize upfront risk by shifting 50% of the consideration to performance-based and time-based milestones, specifically to address the lack of P&L transparency.
structures.suitable_when: Due diligence cannot fully verify the inferred 10% EBITDA margin or if the aging asset base requires immediate heavy CapEx.

consideration.earnout_rationale: Trigger 4 (Unverified add-backs/earnings): The valuation is based on an inferred EBITDA due to missing P&L data. The earnout ensures the buyer only pays for verified, sustainable earnings.

key_conditions: Full P&L audit for the last 3 fiscal years prior to completion
CEO and Divisional MDs must remain in post for the full 36-month earnout period
Working capital peg set at £7.07M (Current Position)
structures.notes: Seller obligations: 12-month full-time handover followed by 24-month consultancy; 3-year non-compete. Warranties: 25% cap on general warranties, 100% on fundamental; 24-month claim period. Completion: Completion accounts mechanism required to verify the high cash and inventory balances. Risk: Low, as the structure protects against the 'missing' P&L data and aging assets.

structures.name: Balanced Approach
structures.strategy: A standard 70/30 split that provides the seller with significant liquidity while retaining enough leverage to ensure a smooth management transition.
structures.suitable_when: Preliminary due diligence confirms the revenue scale and provides reasonable comfort on the gross margin profile.

consideration.earnout_rationale: Trigger 3 (Key person dependency): The CEO's 15-year tenure creates significant institutional knowledge risk. The earnout is tied to a successful 2-year transition and relationship handover.

key_conditions: Appointment of a Group Finance Director within 6 months of completion
Maintenance of QualiCoat accreditation for the powder coating line
Inventory valuation audit to ensure £3.3M stock is current and saleable
structures.notes: Seller obligations: 6-month handover; 2-year non-compete. Warranties: 35% cap; 18-month claim period; £50k basket. Completion: Locked box mechanism could be used if the date is recent, given the strong cash position. Risk: Medium, primarily centered on the transition of the long-tenured CEO and the high working capital intensity.

structures.name: Competitive Approach
structures.strategy: Maximize upfront cash to bridge the gap with seller expectations (£12M-£18M), utilizing the company's own cash reserves to fund the deal.
structures.suitable_when: The buyer is a strategic player who can absorb the manufacturing capacity and has their own finance team to professionalize the target.

consideration.earnout_rationale: No earnout is included to make the offer more attractive in a competitive process, relying instead on a higher upfront payment and fixed deferred amounts.

key_conditions: Specific indemnity for IT and office infrastructure replacement costs
Key man insurance for the CEO during the 12-month handover
structures.notes: Seller obligations: 6-month handover; 2-year non-compete. Warranties: 50% cap; 12-month claim period; higher de minimis. Completion: Completion accounts with a focus on 'Net Debt' and 'Working Capital' definitions. Risk: High, due to the lack of performance-contingent pay and the high upfront multiple on unverified earnings.

recommendation_rationale: The 'Conservative Approach' is recommended primarily because of the 'low' confidence in the valuation caused by missing P&L data. In manufacturing, revenue does not always equal profit, and the high working capital absorption (£7M+) suggests potential inefficiencies. A structure that heavily weights the final price on verified EBITDA performance post-acquisition is the only way to safely bridge the gap between the inferred valuation and the seller's high expectations.
negotiation_priorities: Verification of the 10% EBITDA margin assumption
Agreement on a Working Capital Peg that accounts for the recent £2.6M increase in NWC
Securing a long-term commitment from the divisional MDs
Defining 'Maintenance CapEx' to ensure the aging asset base is managed
deal_breaker_terms: Discovery of significant bad debt within the £2.2M trade debtors
Refusal to provide a full 3-year P&L audit
Departure of more than one divisional MD prior to completion
key_findings: The business is exceptionally liquid but cash-consumptive in its current growth phase.
The 2022 powder coating line is the 'crown jewel' asset, but the rest of the infrastructure is aging.
There is a significant gap between the buyer's EBITDA-based valuation and the seller's likely revenue-based expectations.
The lack of a qualified FD is a major operational risk for a business of this scale.
narrative: Canoports UK Limited is a high-quality manufacturing target with a strong balance sheet, but it suffers from a 'transparency tax' due to missing income statement data. The deal structure must act as a bridge between the impressive balance sheet (nearly £3M cash, £7.8M NAV) and the unverified P&L. By using a Conservative Approach with a 3-year earnout, the buyer can validate the inferred £1.7M EBITDA while ensuring the long-tenured CEO remains incentivized to transition the business. The high working capital peg will be a point of contention, as the seller will likely want to extract the 'excess' cash, while the buyer will need it to fund the heavy stock requirements and aging asset replacement.
